sub_graphs.title: Bellatrix: Validator Block Proposal with Execution Payload
sub_graphs.description: Models the two-step process validators use to prepare and include execution payloads in proposed beacon blocks

nodes.label: Validator Assigned to Slot
nodes.description: Validator has been selected as block proposer for the current slot

nodes.label: Detect Terminal PoW Block
nodes.description: Identify the terminal PoW block by checking terminal total difficulty or terminal block hash override

nodes.label: Terminal PoW Block Identified
nodes.description: The terminal PoW block has been identified, enabling transition payload construction

nodes.label: Prepare Execution Payload
nodes.description: Call execution engine with state info, safe/finalized hashes, and fee recipient to begin payload building; returns payload_id

nodes.label: Execution Payload Building
nodes.description: Execution engine is asynchronously building an execution payload identified by payload_id

nodes.label: Retrieve Execution Payload
nodes.description: Call get_payload(payload_id) on execution engine to retrieve the most recent constructed execution payload

nodes.label: Execution Payload Ready
nodes.description: Execution payload has been retrieved and is ready for inclusion in the beacon block body

nodes.label: Construct Beacon Block
nodes.description: Assemble the full beacon block including the execution payload in the block body

nodes.label: Beacon Block Proposed
nodes.description: Signed beacon block with execution payload has been broadcast to the network

edges.label: Terminal block identified via TTD or override hash
Begin payload preparation with terminal block as parent
Post-merge: prepare payload using latest execution payload header
Include payload in beacon block body

external_entities.name: PoW Chain
external_entities.description: Legacy proof-of-work chain providing terminal block information during the merge transition

external_entities.name: Fork Choice Store

sub_graphs.title: Bellatrix: Block and Attestation Validity Checks
sub_graphs.description: Models the validation requirements that prevent validators from proposing or attesting to invalid blocks

nodes.label: Block Received for Validation
nodes.description: A beacon block has been received and needs validation before attesting

nodes.label: Validate Beacon State Transition
nodes.description: Execute beacon chain state transition function to verify block validity

nodes.label: Validate Execution Payload
nodes.description: Verify execution payload validity through the execution engine

nodes.label: Block Deemed Valid
nodes.description: Block has passed both beacon and execution validation; safe to attest

nodes.label: Block Deemed Invalid
nodes.description: Block failed validation; validator must not propose on or attest to it

edges.label: Beacon valid; proceed to execution validation

external_entities.name: Network Peer
external_entities.description: Peer node that propagated the block via P2P gossip

sub_graphs.title: Bellatrix: Execution Engine Trust Boundary
sub_graphs.description: Models the trust boundary between the consensus layer validator and the execution engine

nodes.label: Fork Choice Data Available
nodes.description: Safe block hash and finalized block hash are available from the fork choice store

nodes.label: Call engine_forkchoiceUpdated
nodes.description: Send fork choice state and payload attributes to the execution engine via Engine API

nodes.label: Execution Engine Syncing
nodes.description: Execution engine reports SYNCING status; payload cannot be built yet

nodes.label: Payload ID Received from Engine
nodes.description: Execution engine accepted the request and returned a payload_id for later retrieval

nodes.label: Call engine_getPayload
nodes.description: Retrieve constructed payload from execution engine using payload_id

nodes.label: Payload Returned by Engine
nodes.description: Execution engine returned the constructed execution payload

edges.label: Pass fork choice state to execution engine

external_entities.name: Execution Engine
external_entities.description: Trusted execution layer client communicating via authenticated Engine API

external_entities.name: Fee Recipient Configuration
external_entities.description: Operator-configured fee recipient address for block rewards

ambiguities.text: get_payload returns the 'most recent' execution payload built since the corresponding fork choice update notification
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume 'most recent' means the payload with the highest cumulative gas used or value, as execution engines may continuously improve payloads. This needs verification against Engine API spec.

ambiguities.text: The spec does not specify behavior when the execution engine is unavailable or returns an error during get_payload
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the validator should skip block proposal for that slot if the execution engine is unreachable. This is an assumption based on safety-first design.

implicit_assumptions.description: The execution engine is trusted to produce valid execution payloads and not include invalid transactions
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A compromised execution engine could cause the validator to propose invalid blocks, leading to slashing or chain corruption.

implicit_assumptions.description: The communication channel between the consensus client and execution engine (Engine API) is authenticated and local
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A man-in-the-middle attacker could inject malicious payloads or redirect block rewards to attacker-controlled addresses.

implicit_assumptions.description: The fee recipient address is correctly configured by the node operator
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Block rewards could be sent to an incorrect or attacker-controlled address if configuration is compromised.
